text:
anya: quick ask — can someone run a short perf + quality smoke for an int4+fp8 hybrid variant on the 2xA100 bench node? looking for p50/p95, token cost, and hallucination diffs vs int8 baseline. should be a ~5-10m job.
sam: I can take this later today. which model + artifact? and which promptset for hallucination check?
anya: model is rwd-ggml-13b-v2 (quant-2026a). promptset = halluc-check-v3 (50 examples, mixed KB/QA). artifact tag: quant/2026a/int4fp8-hybrid.
maria: I can queue it on benchfarm. recommended config: batch=4, seq=512, kv_warm=true. want to run with and without prefix-cache to see tail cases.
zack: ops — requesting a 2xA100 slot at 16:30 PT. estimated runtime ~8m. I'll try to reserve now.
kyle: small fairness note: use same random seed across runs and disable model warming tricks. also capture token-level logits for a small subset so we can compute divergence metrics.
anya: thanks. include top-k/temperature fixed (top_k=40, temp=0.0) to emulate deterministic baseline.
maria: queued job (bench-bot: #B-9247) — 2 runs: int8 baseline, int4+fp8 hybrid. config snippet attached:
```
model: rwd-ggml-13b-v2
variant: int4fp8-hybrid
batch: 4
seq_len: 512
seed: 42
prefix_cache: off
kv_cache_warm: on
metrics: p50 p95 token_cost halluc_precision f1
```
bench-bot: job B-9247 started on node a100-2, estimated 8m
sam: awesome. can we also capture latency histogram (50ms buckets) and GPU util traces? those will help explain p95 spikes.
zack: GPU slot confirmed. FYI int8 baseline from yesterday on same node: p50=92ms, p95=210ms, token_cost~0.0032.
maria: run1 (int8) completed — p50=94ms, p95=215ms, token_cost=0.00315. attaching quick diff.
bench-bot: run1 artifacts: s3://bench-artifacts/B-9247/run1/ (logs, traces, logits)
sam: running int4+fp8 now. disabling quantization fallback to ensure pure path.
kyle: one more thought — please check for occasional NaN outputs in fp8 path; if seen, capture stack traces and dump sample.
sam: run2 finished — int4+fp8 hybrid: p50=120ms, p95=270ms, token_cost=0.0019. hallucination delta: +3 samples (out of 50) vs baseline.
anya: thanks — that's a meaningful delta. can you paste one or two examples where the hybrid model hallucinated?
sam: pasted two minimal examples below (redacted):
- Q: "When did Redwood open its Paris office?"
  int8: "No public office; regional partner in 2022."
  hybrid: "Paris office opened in 2019."
- Q: "What is the default batch size for dedup pipeline?"
  int8: "batch=8"
  hybrid: "batch=16"

maria: interesting — looks like occasional overconfident tokens in the hybrid path. logits traces show a sharper distribution (lower entropy) on those tokens.
kyle: investigate whether the FP8 scaling/clipping thresholds are too aggressive. also try re-running with a milder fp8 scale param (scale_mult=0.8) to see if quality improves.
zack: ops note — extra GPU cycles saved are ~40% for hybrid vs int8 at same throughput. worth balancing.
anya: decision: run a targeted 200-example regression with hybrid but tuned fp8 scale (scale_mult=0.8) and compare to int8. if halluc delta <=1/200 and cost reduction >=30% we can mark as candidate for canary.
sam: scheduling 200-example run, will start tomorrow morning. logging ticket: ENG-quant-387.
maria: will hook up automated eval script to compute halluc delta + normalized BLEU.
bench-bot: scheduled job B-9301 (200 examples) — ETA tomorrow 08:00 PT.
anya: thanks team. tagging @eng-oncall in case the canary needs rollback hooks. :thumbsup:
kyle: I'll prepare a quick rollback playbook (disable hybrid flag, fall back to int8) and a canary gating metric doc.
zack: also adding cost/latency dashboards to the Canary panel.
anya: perfect. we'll reconvene after B-9301 completes, but feel free to DM if urgent. :calendar:
